distros.name: Linux Mint
distros.description: Looks and feels like Windows. Everything works right after install.

distros.name: Ubuntu
distros.description: The most popular Linux. You can find help for any problem.

distros.name: Pop!_OS
distros.description: Based on Ubuntu, with NVIDIA drivers ready and built-in tiling.

distros.name: Debian
distros.description: Very stable. The software is older, but it almost never breaks.

distros.name: Fedora
distros.description: New software and a clean desktop. Great for programming.

distros.name: openSUSE Tumbleweed
distros.description: Always up to date, with automatic snapshots if an update fails.

distros.name: Manjaro
distros.description: Based on Arch, with a graphical installer and ready-made desktops.

distros.name: EndeavourOS
distros.description: Almost pure Arch with an easy installer. Great for ricing.

distros.name: Arch Linux
distros.description: You build the system piece by piece. The best wiki in the Linux world.

packages.name: Hyprland
packages.description: A modern tiling window manager for Wayland, with animations and rounded corners.
packages.why: The most popular choice for ricing: it looks great and everything is set in one config file.

packages.name: Sway
packages.description: A simple and stable tiling window manager for Wayland.
packages.why: It works on almost every distro, so it is a calm first step into tiling.

packages.name: BSPWM
packages.description: A tiling window manager for X11, controlled with shell commands.
packages.why: Good for older laptops and for people who like to script everything.

packages.name: Waybar
packages.description: The status bar at the top of the screen, for Wayland.
packages.why: Shows the clock, battery, Wi-Fi and workspaces. You style it with CSS, like a web page.

packages.name: Polybar
packages.description: A status bar for X11 window managers.
packages.why: The classic bar for BSPWM and i3 setups.

packages.name: Rofi
packages.description: An app launcher: press a key, type a name, open the app.
packages.why: A tiling window manager has no start menu. Rofi is the start menu.

packages.name: Wofi
packages.description: A small app launcher made for Wayland.
packages.why: A light alternative to Rofi for Hyprland and Sway.

packages.name: Dunst
packages.description: Shows small notification pop-ups.
packages.why: Without it you never see messages like 'battery low' in a tiling setup.

packages.name: Feh
packages.description: An image viewer that can also set your wallpaper.
packages.why: The easiest way to put a wallpaper on an X11 desktop.

packages.name: Zsh
packages.description: A shell: the program that reads the commands you type.
packages.why: Better autocomplete than Bash and lots of themes (Oh My Zsh).

packages.name: Fish
packages.description: A friendly shell that suggests commands while you type.
packages.why: Perfect for beginners: it is helpful with zero configuration.

packages.name: Alacritty
packages.description: A fast terminal that uses your graphics card.
packages.why: Simple, fast and configured with a single text file.

packages.name: Kitty
packages.description: A fast terminal with tabs, splits and image previews.
packages.why: Very popular in riced setups, with hundreds of ready-made themes.

packages.name: Foot
packages.description: A tiny and very fast terminal for Wayland.
packages.why: Starts instantly and uses almost no memory.

packages.name: Tmux
packages.description: Splits one terminal into many panes and keeps your work open.
packages.why: Very useful when you work on a server over SSH.

packages.name: Btop
packages.description: Shows CPU, memory, disk and running programs.
packages.why: It is the Linux Task Manager, only prettier.

packages.name: Fastfetch
packages.description: Prints your distro logo and system info in the terminal.
packages.why: The screenshot every ricer posts. Also a quick way to see your hardware.

packages.name: Fzf
packages.description: Fuzzy search for files and for your command history.
packages.why: Press Ctrl+R and find any old command in one second.

packages.name: Ripgrep
packages.description: Searches text inside files, very fast.
packages.why: A faster and simpler grep.

packages.name: Neovim
packages.description: A text editor that runs inside the terminal.
packages.why: Fast, works everywhere and can grow into a full code editor.

packages.name: VLC
packages.description: Plays almost any video or audio file.
packages.why: Opens the files that other players refuse to open.

packages.name: MPV
packages.description: A minimal video player controlled from the keyboard.
packages.why: Light and fits perfectly in a tiling setup.

packages.name: GIMP
packages.description: An image editor, a free alternative to Photoshop.
packages.why: Edit photos or make your own wallpapers.

packages.name: OBS Studio
packages.description: Records or streams your screen.
packages.why: Record your desktop to show off your rice.

packages.name: Thunar
packages.description: A light file manager with windows and icons.
packages.why: Tiling window managers come without a file manager. Thunar is fast and simple.

packages.name: Yazi
packages.description: A file manager inside the terminal, with image previews.
packages.why: Move through your files with the keyboard, very fast.

packages.name: Git
packages.description: Saves the history of your files and talks to GitHub.
packages.why: Almost every dotfiles repo and coding project needs it.

packages.name: Curl
packages.description: Downloads files from the internet, from the terminal.
packages.why: Many install guides start with a curl command.

packages.name: Flatpak
packages.description: A second app store that works on every distro.
packages.why: Gets you apps like Spotify or Discord even when your distro does not have them.

packages.name: Timeshift
packages.description: Takes snapshots of your system so you can go back in time.
packages.why: If an update breaks something, you restore yesterday's system in minutes.

packages.name: UFW
packages.description: A simple firewall.
packages.why: One command (sudo ufw enable) blocks unwanted connections.
